comparisons.peer_topic: Grants Receivable Carrying Value and Fair Value
comparisons.peer_summary: The aggregate carrying value of grants receivable was $1.7 billion as of December 28, 2024, compared to $559 million in the prior year, with fair value estimated to approximate carrying value and classified as Level 2.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and INTC disclose that the fair value of specific financial assets or contract components approximates their carrying values, but they apply this principle to fundamentally different asset classes. AVGO applies this valuation approach to the 'off-market component of customer contracts' (rebates and marketing development funds) resulting from the VMware Merger, stating that the remaining unamortized balances approximate fair value. In contrast, INTC applies this approximation to 'grants receivable,' asserting that the estimated fair value of these financial assets approximates their carrying value. While both disclosures utilize the concept of carrying value approximating fair value, the underlying subject matter differs: AVGO's relates to acquired customer contract economics, whereas INTC's relates to government grant receivables.

sentences.text: We valued these contracts based on their remaining unamortized balances, which approximate their fair value.
The estimated fair value of these financial assets approximates their carrying value.
